subject: protection-record
evidence: Branch protection and rulesets are unavailable on claude.agent.core: private repository, account plan 'free' (gh api user --jq .plan.name). FIVE CALLS, each made once, no retry loop, at 2026-09-22T23:15:42Z: PUT repos/JerryBalmer1/claude.agent.core/branches/main/protection; the same for develop; POST repos/JerryBalmer1/claude.agent.core/rulesets (ruleset core-flow targeting refs/heads/main and refs/heads/develop with deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request and required_status_checks over the six names in config/repo.json required_checks); and read-backs of branches/main/protection and rulesets. All five returned HTTP 403 'Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.' Repository settings read back after and UNCHANGED by all five: {deleteBranchOnMerge:true, mergeCommitAllowed:true, rebaseMergeAllowed:false, squashMergeAllowed:false}. 403 IS NOT 404: a 404 would mean the feature exists and the branch is unprotected, which a person can fix; a 403 is the tier declining to offer it, and no toggle reachable from this account changes it. SUBSTRATE'S CONFOUND DOES NOT APPLY: its PROTECTION.md noted develop did not exist on origin when its call was made, so its 403 could have stood in for a 404. Core's develop existed on origin before this call, pushed at birth and merged into twice since. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TAG: anything pinning v0.2.0^{commit} - images as a submodule, tools at Phase 0 - inherits a main that nothing server-side refuses to rewrite. The controls that remain are push-guard (after the fact; it cannot refuse a push, only make it loud and dated), the flow rules in AGENTS.md (convention), and the merge-method lock (the one real server-side refusal, reversible with one gh repo edit). Recorded as FINDINGS F80 BEFORE the tag is cut, not after. docs/PROTECTION.md rewritten from substrate's inherited transcripts to core's own measurements; BACKLOG B12 closes both when the account is Pro or the repo is public and the three calls succeed unchanged.
